usage: This is the standard, everyday way to ask the price of an item in Cairo. It is used in all contexts, from street markets to high-end stores, regardless of who you are speaking to. The demonstrative pronoun changes based on the grammatical gender of the item being discussed.

variants.label: feminine item
variants.note: Use when pointing at a grammatically feminine object like a bag or a car.

variants.label: plural items
variants.note: Use when asking the price of multiple items together.

variants.label: polite to a man
variants.note: Add 'law sama7t' to be more polite to a male shopkeeper.

variants.label: polite to a woman
variants.note: Add 'law sama7ti' to be more polite to a female shopkeeper.

examples.english: Excuse me, how much is this?
How much is this? It is very expensive!
